context: Current closing price of Deere (DE): $529.90 USD as of 2026-05-22.
justification_text:
My point estimates across all three horizons reflect a relatively stable, modestly upward-drifting baseline. For the 1-day estimate around 531.5, I was anchoring heavily on the most recent price level and assuming mean-reversion tendencies would dominate over such a short window, with only marginal drift expected. The 1-week estimate of 533 reflects a slight continuation of that drift while acknowledging that intraday noise averages out somewhat. The 1-month estimate of 535 assumes a continuation of the prevailing trend but with diminishing confidence in any specific directional movement — essentially the drift component of a random walk process over roughly 22 trading days.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated using historical volatility as the primary input, scaled appropriately to each time horizon via the square-root-of-time rule. For the 1-day window, realized short-term volatility is relatively constrained, hence the tighter 516–547 range. Over a week, idiosyncratic events, earnings announcements, or macro data releases can accumulate, widening the interval to 505–561. The 1-month range of 480–592 reflects the compounding of these uncertainties across a longer period, where regime shifts and sustained trends have more time to develop and deviate materially from the starting point.

There are meaningful tail risks that could push outcomes outside even these wider intervals. On the downside, an unexpected deterioration in macroeconomic conditions — such as a sharper-than-expected inflation print, a Federal Reserve policy surprise, or a geopolitical shock — could drive prices well below 480 over the month. Conversely, a strong risk-on rally driven by positive earnings surprises, a dovish policy pivot, or easing financial conditions could push prices above 592.

It is also worth noting that the structure of the underlying asset or index matters here. If this represents an equity index or individual stock with elevated implied volatility in options markets, my intervals may actually be too narrow. Liquidity conditions, short-term positioning dynamics, and technical breakouts near key support or resistance levels could all trigger non-linear moves that a simple volatility-scaled model would underestimate.
